hints: Look closely at time X and compare the solid ventricle line with the aorta line, which one is rising fast and about to go higher?
Remember valves open when pressure behind them is higher than in front, and think about what the atria do while the ventricles are contracting.
walkthrough:
**Spot what is happening at time X**

Look at the three pressure lines at X. The ventricle pressure (solid line) is shooting up steeply and is just reaching the aorta pressure (dash-dot line).

Atrium pressure (dotted line) is very low, near $0 \text{ kPa}$.

**Decide about the aortic semilunar valve**

The rule is simple: a valve opens when pressure behind it is greater than pressure in front of it.

$$\text{if ventricular pressure} > \text{aortic pressure, then aortic valve opens}$$ 
Just after X, ventricle exceeds aorta, so the valve is opening to let blood into the aorta. This is the start of ventricular systole.

**Decide about the atrium**

During ventricular systole the atria are relaxed in diastole. The AV valves are closed, so blood returning from veins collects in the atria.

That means the atrium is filling, not emptying. Opening valve plus filling atrium matches D.

options.A: Closing is wrong because ventricular pressure is rising above aortic pressure, which opens the valve. Emptying is wrong because the atrium fills during ventricular systole.
options.B: Closing is wrong, this is the start of ejection when the valve opens. Filling is correct for the atrium, but the valve part makes this option wrong.
options.C: Opening is correct, but emptying is wrong. The atrium does not contract now, it relaxes and fills with venous blood while the ventricle contracts.
options.D: Correct. Ventricle pressure exceeds aorta pressure at X so the aortic semilunar valve opens, and the relaxed atrium is filling with blood at the same time.
